title: Talking With Patients: Rapport and Interviews

slides.title: Today's lesson
slides.body:
As an EMR you already introduce yourself, calm frightened people and take a history. Now, as a PCP:

  1. Build rapport fast, and use your first words as a mental status check
  2. Run a sharper interview: question types and six techniques
  3. Handle hard situations, and see how talking drives PCP decisions

Textbook: Chapter 10, PDF pages 760–798
slides.say: Welcome. Today's topic sounds soft, but it's a real clinical skill. As an EMR you already introduce yourself, calm frightened people, and take a history. So why study it again? Because as a PCP, more decisions hang on what the patient tells you. Every drug you give depends on allergies, medications and history, and a missed answer can mean a wrong drug. Talking is also how you check the brain and earn trust before a needle goes in. Today we'll cover three things: building rapport fast, running a sharper interview, and handling hard situations.
slides.sayZh: 欢迎。今天的主题听起来很软，但它是真正的临床技能。作为 EMR，你已经会自我介绍、安抚受惊的人、采集病史。那为什么还要再学？因为作为 PCP，更多决定取决于病人告诉你的内容。你给的每一种药都取决于过敏、用药和病史，漏问一个答案就可能给错药。交谈也是你检查大脑功能、在扎针之前赢得信任的方式。今天讲三件事：快速建立融洽关系，进行更精准的问诊，以及处理棘手的情况。

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.body:
The patient is why we exist, not a problem to solve

  • You often meet people on their worst day
  • Being invited into a home is a privilege
  • Family members are scared too: include them
  • Total patient care = physical, mental and emotional needs
slides.say: Let's start with attitude. The textbook reminds us that the S in EMS stands for service. The patient isn't a puzzle or an interruption; the patient is the reason we exist. You'll often meet people on their worst day, sometimes covered in vomit, blood or urine; accepting that without complaint is part of the job. Many of your calls take you into someone's home, so treat it as a privilege. Remember the family, too. They're frightened, and ignoring them is a real failure of care. Total patient care means meeting physical, mental and emotional needs, for the patient and the people around them.
slides.sayZh: 先说态度。教材提醒我们，EMS 里的 S 代表服务。病人不是谜题，也不是打扰，病人就是我们存在的理由。你常会在别人最糟糕的一天见到他们，有时满身呕吐物、血或尿；毫无怨言地接受，本就是工作的一部分。很多出车会进入别人的家，要把这当作一种荣幸。也要记住家属。他们很害怕，忽视他们是照护上的真正失职。全面照护是指照顾身体、精神和情感的需要，既包括病人，也包括他身边的人。

slides.title: Your first ten seconds
slides.body:
1. Say your full name and that you are a paramedic
  2. Ask the patient's name; use the formality they choose
  3. Watch how they answer

To answer, the patient must hear, find your voice, understand, remember and speak, all in about 1 second: a mini mental status exam.
slides.say: Your opening matters. Before asking what's wrong, introduce yourself with your full name and say you're a paramedic. Then ask the patient's name, and use the level of formality they choose. If he says he's Mr. Chen, don't call him buddy. Here's a hidden bonus: asking a name is a mini mental status exam. To answer, the patient must hear you, turn toward your voice and make eye contact, understand, pull the answer from memory, and say it clearly, all in about one second. Up close, you can check the pupils too. So your polite greeting is already part of your neurological assessment.
slides.sayZh: 开场很重要。在问哪里不舒服之前，先报出你的全名，说明你是 paramedic。然后问病人的名字，并按他自己选的正式程度称呼他。如果他说自己是陈先生，就别叫他「哥们」。这里有个隐藏的好处：问名字就是一次迷你精神状态检查。病人要回答，必须听见你、转向你的声音并和你对视、理解问题、从记忆里找出答案、再清楚地说出来，这一切大约在一秒内完成。离得近，还能顺便看瞳孔。所以你礼貌的问候，已经是神经系统评估的一部分。

slides.title: Building rapport
slides.body:
• Fear: stay calm and competent, care honestly, explain findings and plan
  • Pain: acknowledge it and relieve it as soon as you can
  • Modesty: cover the patient, even in a rush
  • No judging: someone who lies is a "poor historian", not a bad person
  • Professional skepticism helps; cynicism hurts
slides.say: Rapport means trust between you and the patient, and you can't fake it; people in crisis notice. Your tone of voice matters as much as your words. Handle fear three ways: be calm and competent, care honestly, and give information, like your findings and your plan. Acknowledge pain, and relieve it as soon as your protocols allow. Protect modesty by covering the patient, even when you're rushing. And don't judge. Some patients lie, often out of stress or fear. Treat them as a poor historian, meaning an unreliable source, and keep asking. Healthy doubt about the history is useful; bitter cynicism is not.
slides.sayZh: 融洽关系是指你和病人之间的信任，它装不出来，处在危机中的人一眼就看得出。你的语调和你的话语一样重要。化解恐惧有三种方法：沉着胜任、真诚关心、给他信息，比如你的发现和你的计划。要承认病人的疼痛，并在流程允许时尽快缓解。即使再赶时间，也要给病人遮盖，保护他的体面。还有，不要评判。有些病人会说谎，往往是出于压力或恐惧。把他当作「不可靠的病史提供者」，继续问下去。对病史保持合理的怀疑是有益的，愤世嫉俗则不是。

slides.title: Listening on a noisy scene
slides.body:
• Active listening: repeat back the key part of each answer
  • Write answers down: don't make them repeat themselves
  • Don't shout: cut the noise, get close, move to the ambulance
  • Ask private questions in a private place
  • Don't assume an older person can't hear: start at normal volume
  • "Thank you" → "You're welcome", not "No problem"
slides.say: Active listening means repeating back the important part of each answer. It shows you're listening, and it catches misunderstandings. Write answers down, so the patient never has to repeat them. On a noisy scene, don't shout; if you shout, everyone shouts. Ask for the music to be turned off, move close, speak calmly, and get the patient into the ambulance soon. Sensitive questions belong in a quiet, private place. Don't assume an older patient is hard of hearing; start at a normal volume. And small words count: when a patient thanks you, say you're welcome, not no problem, which hints they almost were one.
slides.sayZh: 主动倾听是指把每个回答里的关键部分复述一遍。这表明你在听，也能发现误解。把回答记下来，让病人不必重复。现场嘈杂时不要喊，你一喊，大家都跟着喊。请人关掉音乐，靠近病人，平静地说话，尽快把病人移到救护车里。敏感问题要在安静、私密的地方问。别默认老人耳背，先用正常音量说话。小词也很重要：病人向你道谢时，说「不客气」，不要说「没问题」，后者暗示他差一点就成了麻烦。

slides.q: You're called to a crowded, noisy bar for a man who collapsed. He's sitting up but seems confused. What is your best first step?
options: Shout your questions so he can hear you over the music
Introduce yourself, ask his name and watch how he answers
Ask his friends how much he drank, since he's clearly drunk
Start straight away with your standard history questions
slides.say: Quiz time. You're called to a crowded, noisy bar for a man who collapsed. He's sitting up but seems confused. What is your best first step? A, shout your questions so he can hear you over the music. B, introduce yourself, ask his name, and watch how he answers. C, ask his friends how much he drank, since he's clearly drunk. D, start straight away with your standard history questions. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 测验时间。你被叫到一家拥挤嘈杂的酒吧，一名男子晕倒了。他已经坐起来，但看起来有些糊涂。你最好的第一步是什么？A，大声喊着提问，好让他在音乐声中听见。B，自我介绍，问他的名字，并观察他怎么回答。C，问他的朋友他喝了多少，因为他显然喝醉了。D，直接开始问你那套标准病史问题。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. Introducing yourself and asking his name builds trust and doubles as a mini mental status check: can he hear, understand and answer within about a second? Then ask staff to cut the noise and move him to the ambulance. A raises everyone's volume and tension. C is the assumption trap: confusion can come from low blood sugar, low oxygen or a head injury, not just alcohol. D skips the introduction and tells you nothing yet about his mental status.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。自我介绍并问他的名字，既能建立信任，又是一次迷你精神状态检查：他能不能在大约一秒内听见、理解并回答？然后请店员降低噪音，把他移到救护车里。A 会让所有人的音量和紧张都升高。C 掉进了想当然的陷阱：糊涂可能来自低血糖、缺氧或头部外伤，不只是酒精。D 跳过了自我介绍，也还没告诉你任何关于他精神状态的信息。

slides.title: Three kinds of questions
slides.body:
Open-ended“Tell me about the pain.”no options, no yes/no
Closed-ended“Any heart problems?”history, specific facts
Payoff“Has anything been worrying you?”may reveal the real reason

Don't offer choices like “sharp or dull?”: let the patient find the word.
slides.say: There are three kinds of questions. Open-ended questions can't be answered with yes or no, and they don't offer choices. Tell me about the pain lets the patient use their own words, which are usually more accurate. Ask is it sharp or dull, and you've put words in their mouth. Closed-ended questions get specific facts, like past history: any heart problems, diabetes, seizures? Use plain words, not medical terms. Payoff questions are like the tip of an iceberg; a small question can reveal the hidden reason you were called. For example: has anything been worrying you lately? Or, in private: is anyone hurting you?
slides.sayZh: 问题分三种。开放式问题不能用是或否回答，也不提供选项。「说说你的疼痛」让病人用自己的话描述，通常更准确。你要是问「是刺痛还是钝痛」，就等于把话塞进了他嘴里。封闭式问题用来获取具体事实，比如既往史：有没有心脏问题、糖尿病、癫痫？用通俗的话，不用医学术语。关键问题就像冰山一角，一个小问题可能揭开你被叫来的真正原因。比如：最近有什么事让你担心吗？或者在私下问：有人在伤害你吗？

slides.title: Six ways to get a useful answer
slides.body:
TechniqueWhat you do
Facilitate“Please tell me more.”
Silencewait a few seconds
Clarifyask them to explain
Redirectbring them back to the question
Interpretsay what you think they mean
Simplify and summarizerestate it simply: “Is that right?”
slides.say: People in crisis are often poor communicators, so you need tools. Facilitate: if they hesitate, encourage them to say more. Silence: if they're searching for words, say nothing for a few seconds. Clarify: if you don't understand, ask them to explain. Redirect: if they skip a question, politely bring them back to it, more than once if needed. Interpret: if you're still unsure, say what you think they mean and let them correct you. Simplify and summarize: turn a confused answer into a simple sentence and ask if it's right. And if you must interrupt to do something urgent, explain why, and promise to listen when you're done.
slides.sayZh: 处在危机中的人往往不善表达，所以你需要工具。促进：他犹豫时，鼓励他多说一点。沉默：他在找词的时候，几秒钟什么都别说。澄清：没听懂就请他解释。重新引导：他跳过某个问题时，礼貌地把他拉回来，必要时多拉几次。解释：还是不确定，就说出你理解的意思，让他纠正。简化与总结：把混乱的回答换成一句简单的话，问他对不对。如果你必须打断他去做紧急的事，要说明原因，并承诺做完再听他说。

slides.title: Common interviewing errors
slides.body:
• Assuming: “faking”, “drunk”, “his wife”: stay open
  • Giving medical advice: send them to their doctor
  • False hope: be honest, but kind
  • Acting like the police
  • Hiding the truth: share vitals, glucose, your impression
  • Professional distancing: jargon and half-answers
slides.say: Now the common errors. The biggest is assuming: that a patient is faking, that someone is drunk, or that their companion is a spouse. Keep an open mind. Don't give medical advice or judge their doctor's decisions; suggest they ask their doctor. Don't give false hope. A stable patient asking if they'll die deserves a calm, honest, gentle answer. But a patient who looks you in the eye and says they're dying is often right: act fast, and let the family say goodbye. Don't act like a police officer, don't hide the truth, and avoid jargon and half-answers that keep the patient at a distance.
slides.sayZh: 下面是常见错误。最大的错误是想当然：认定病人在装、认定某人喝醉了，或认定陪同的人是配偶。要保持开放的心态。不要给医疗建议，也不要评判他医生的决定，建议他去问自己的医生。不要给虚假的希望。稳定的病人问自己会不会死，应得到平静、诚实、温和的回答。但如果病人直视你说他要死了，他往往是对的，所以要快速行动，让家属有机会道别。不要摆出警察的架势，不要隐瞒真相，也要避免用术语和半真半假的回答把病人推远。

slides.title: Nonverbal skills
slides.body:
Eyesbrief, frequent eye contactat their eye level
Touchask, then shoulder or armstop if they pull away
Posturecrouch, at an angleno crossed arms

Culture changes the rules: in many cultures, avoiding eye contact shows respect. Ask before you touch.
slides.say: Much of what you communicate isn't words. Most patients expect brief, frequent, direct eye contact, which shows honesty and care. Get down to their eye level, especially with children or someone in bed or a wheelchair. Touch can calm someone, but explain and ask first, for example: "Is it okay if I touch your shoulder?" If they agree, use a light touch on the shoulder or arm. Watch the response: if they pull away, stop. Don't stand over a frightened patient with your arms crossed. Crouch or sit at their level or lower, at an angle, outside their personal space. But culture changes the rules. In many Asian, African and Latin American cultures, avoiding eye contact shows respect. So follow the patient's lead, and stay curious, not offended.
slides.sayZh: 你传达的很多信息不是靠语言。大多数病人期待短暂、频繁、直接的目光接触，这传达诚实和关心。要放低到和他视线齐平，尤其是对儿童、卧床或坐轮椅的人。触碰能让人平静下来，但要先解释并征得同意，比如：「我碰一下你的肩膀可以吗？」他同意了，再轻触肩膀或手臂。观察反应：他躲开就停。不要抱着手臂站在受惊的病人面前俯视他。蹲下或坐下，和他齐平或更低，从斜角接近，不侵入他的个人空间。但文化会改变规则。在许多亚洲、非洲和拉美文化里，回避对视是表示尊重。所以要跟着病人的反应走，保持好奇，而不是觉得被冒犯。

slides.title: Talking is a brain check
slides.body:
• Spontaneous, appropriate humour = the highest mental function
  • Simple questions answered in about 1 second
  • Oriented to person, place, day and event
  • Able to follow simple commands

A wrong answer is a finding, not a nuisance: it may mean poor blood flow to the brain.
slides.say: Every conversation is also a brain check, and the textbook gives four clues. First, spontaneous, appropriate humour is the highest level of mental function; a confused brain can't make a good joke. Second, timing: a clear-thinking patient answers a simple question in about one second. Third, orientation: can they tell you who they are and who you are, where they are, what day it is, and what happened? A wrong answer suggests a memory problem and possibly reduced blood flow to the brain. Fourth, can they follow simple commands? If not, think of a brain problem, new or long-standing.
slides.sayZh: 每次交谈也是一次大脑检查，教材给了四条线索。第一，自发而得体的幽默是最高级的精神功能，糊涂的大脑讲不出好笑话。第二，反应时间：思维清楚的病人大约一秒内就能回答简单问题。第三，定向力：他能否说出自己是谁、你是谁、身在何处、今天星期几、发生了什么？答错提示记忆障碍，也可能是脑部血流减少。第四，他能否执行简单指令？不能的话，要考虑大脑出了问题，可能是新发的，也可能是原有的。

slides.q: A 15-year-old girl has abdominal pain. Her father insists on staying for every question and keeps answering for her. What is the best approach?
options: Tell the father he must leave, because teens have a right to privacy
Let him stay, talk to her as an adult, offer choices, tell the ED physician and document it
Take the whole history from the father, since he is the parent
Refuse to continue the assessment until he leaves
slides.say: Second question. A fifteen-year-old girl has abdominal pain. Her father insists on staying for every question and keeps answering for her. What is the best approach? A, tell the father he must leave, because teens have a right to privacy. B, let him stay, talk to her as an adult, offer choices, tell the emergency department physician, and document it. C, take the whole history from the father, since he is the parent. D, refuse to continue the assessment until he leaves. Tap your answer.
slides.sayZh: 第二题。一名十五岁女孩腹痛。她父亲坚持旁听每一个问题，还不停替她回答。最好的做法是什么？A，告诉父亲必须离开，因为青少年有隐私权。B，让他留下，把女孩当成年人来交流，给她选择，告诉急诊医生并记录下来。C，所有病史都问父亲，因为他是家长。D，拒绝继续评估，直到他离开。点选你的答案。
slides.explain: The answer is B. The book's advice: don't refuse a parent's right to be there, but a parent who insists on monitoring every word should raise questions in your mind. Treat the teen as an adult, offer options you can honour, protect her modesty, then tell the emergency department physician and document it accurately. A and D create conflict and delay care. C ignores your actual patient.
slides.explainZh: 答案是 B。书里的建议是：不要拒绝家长在场的权利，但一个坚持监听每一句话的家长应该引起你的怀疑。把青少年当成年人对待，给她你能兑现的选择，保护她的体面，然后告诉急诊医生，并如实记录。A 和 D 制造冲突、耽误救治。C 忽视了你真正的病人。

slides.title: Hard situations
slides.body:
PatientApproach
Quiet, won't talkeye contact, explain each step, keep inviting
Hostilenever argue back; police if out of control
Older adultdon't assume; adapt to hearing, vision, mobility
Young childget low, move gently; involve the parent
Teen (12 and up)treat as an adult; offer real choices
Language barrierapproved interpreter (PHSA Language Link); family only supports
slides.say: Some interviews are harder. A quiet patient with normal mental status shouldn't be forced; keep eye contact, explain each step, and keep inviting them to talk. A hostile patient may swear at you, especially with drugs or alcohol involved. Never argue back; nothing escalates faster. Clenched fists, a hard stare, and heavy breathing through clenched teeth warn of an attack; if it gets out of control, police take over. Don't assume older adults are hard to talk to. With small children, get low, move slowly, and involve the parent. Treat teenagers, from age twelve, like adults. And with a language barrier, use an approved interpreter service first; BCEHS names PHSA Language Link. Family can help and comfort, but they shouldn't be your only interpreter.
slides.sayZh: 有些问诊更难。精神状态正常、却不愿说话的病人不要勉强：保持目光接触，解释每一步，并不断邀请他开口。有敌意的病人可能会骂你，尤其是受药物或酒精影响时。绝不回骂，那是让局面升级最快的方式。握紧拳头、死死盯着你、咬紧牙关粗重呼吸，都是要动手的信号；局面失控时交给警察。别默认老人难沟通。对小孩要放低身体、动作放慢，让家长参与。对十二岁起的青少年，要像对待成年人一样。遇到语言障碍，先用正规的口译服务，BCEHS 指定的是 PHSA Language Link。家属可以帮忙、给安慰，但不应该是唯一的翻译。

slides.title: What the PCP actually does
slides.body:
• Explain before every needle, and warn about the stick
  • Small child: let a parent help steady the arm for the IV
  • Share findings honestly (BP, ECG, glucose); say you're not a doctor
  • Report fully to the physician and read back the order
  • Document concerns (e.g. the insisting parent) and tell the ED

BC grading criteria, pain history: OPQRRRST or LOTARP
slides.say: So what does communication look like in a PCP's day? You now do invasive things, so explain before every needle and warn about the stick. With a small child, let a parent help steady the arm while you start the IV. Share your findings, like the blood pressure, the ECG or the glucose, honestly, while making clear you're not a doctor. When you call a physician, give a complete report and read back the order: drug, dose and route. Document anything unusual, like a parent who won't leave, and tell the emergency department. And when your BC exam patient has pain, the grading criteria expect OPQRRRST or LOTARP to explore it.
slides.sayZh: 那么在 PCP 的日常工作中，沟通是什么样子？你现在要做有创操作，所以每次扎针前都要解释，并提醒会有刺痛。对小孩，开静脉时让家长帮忙扶稳手臂。如实告诉病人你的发现，比如血压、心电图或血糖，同时说明你不是医生。打电话给医生时，要报全病情，并复述医嘱：药名、剂量和途径。记录任何不寻常的情况，比如不肯离开的家长，并告诉急诊科。BC 考试中病人有疼痛时，评分手册要求用 OPQRRRST 或 LOTARP 口诀把疼痛问清楚。

slides.title: New for you as a PCP: watch out for
slides.body:
• New drugs bring new questions: a missed one can mean a wrong drug
  • TXA: when did the injury happen? (not after 3 hours)
  • Ondansetron: personal or family long QT? Pregnancy?
  • Dimenhydrinate, diphenhydramine, ipratropium: ask about glaucoma
  • Ask awkward questions privately, plainly, without judgment
  • Pain you could relieve but don't: poor care and a legal risk
slides.say: Here's what's new to watch for. Your new PCP drugs bring new questions, and a missed answer can mean a wrong drug. Before TXA, you need to know when the injury happened, because BC says not after three hours. Before ondansetron, ask about a personal or family history of long QT syndrome, a heart rhythm problem, and about pregnancy. Before dimenhydrinate, diphenhydramine or ipratropium, ask about glaucoma. Some of these questions feel awkward, so ask them privately, plainly and without judgment. And remember: ignoring pain you could relieve is poor care, and the book warns it can even be grounds for a lawsuit.
slides.sayZh: 下面是你需要新注意的。PCP 的新药带来新的问题，漏问一个答案就可能给错药。给 TXA 前，你要知道受伤是什么时候发生的，因为 BC 规定超过三小时不能给。给昂丹司琼前，要问本人或家族有没有长 QT 综合征（一种心律问题），以及是否怀孕。给茶苯海明、苯海拉明或异丙托溴铵前，要问有没有青光眼。有些问题让人尴尬，所以要私下问、问得直接、不带评判。还要记住：能缓解却不缓解疼痛，是失职的照护，书里还提醒这甚至可能成为被起诉的理由。

slides.title: Three things to remember
slides.body:
1. Open with your name and theirs: it builds trust and checks the brain
  2. Open-ended first, closed for history, payoff for the hidden reason
  3. No assumptions or false hope; your interview drives your drugs

Next: Chapter 11, Research and Quality
slides.say: Let's wrap up with three things to remember. One: open every call with your full name and the patient's name. It builds trust, and it's a quick mental status check. Two: start with open-ended questions, use closed-ended ones for the history, and don't forget payoff questions, which may reveal the real reason you were called. Three: avoid the classic errors, assumptions, false hope, and arguing with a hostile patient. And remember, as a PCP your interview drives your drug decisions. Next class, we move to Chapter eleven, research and quality. If anything was unclear, tap Ask. See you next class.
slides.sayZh: 收尾三句话。一，每次出车都以你的全名和病人的名字开场，既建立信任，又是一次快速的精神状态检查。二，先问开放式问题，病史用封闭式问题，别忘了关键问题，它可能揭开你被叫来的真正原因。三，避开经典错误：想当然、虚假希望、和有敌意的病人对骂。还要记住，作为 PCP，你的问诊决定你的用药。下节课进入第 11 章，研究与质量。有不懂的点「Ask」。下节课见。
